result:
I've saved the Q3 results to `/work/answer.json`. Using the same method, my Q2 calculation reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

**What I had to decide to get the Q2 values to match:**
- **Timestamps:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (with a `Z` suffix). Only after converting to Korea time (UTC+9) and then assigning quarters and months did Q2 match. Using UTC as-is gave a different a_net, b, f, g and h.
- **Customers:** there are 300 customer rows but only 250 unique emails. Counting customers by normalized email (lowercased, spaces trimmed) gives b=233 and f=190 for Q2, which match. Counting by `id` gives 278 and 209, which don't.
- **Segments and categories:** some values differ only by case or spacing (`SMB`, ` consumer`, `Enterprise `), so I lowercased and trimmed them before grouping.
- **Data checks:** every refund matches an order line, and no refund quantity exceeds the quantity ordered.

**Q3 results (July 1 – September 30, 2025, Korea time):**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment / net sales | smb / 289,375,597 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 249 |
| c. Top category / net sales | svc / 251,013,953 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | u33@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 238 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 684,190 |
| h. Change, Sep vs Aug | -17.9% |

Q3 is more sensitive to the time zone than Q2: in UTC the top month would be 2025-09 and h would be +0.9%. Since only the Korea-time approach reproduced Q2, I used it here as well.
